      "informal_description": "For any natural number $ n $, the Roth number function $ \\text{rothNumberNat}(n) $, which gives the maximum size of a subset of $ \\{0, 1, \\ldots, n-1\\} $ containing no three distinct elements forming an arithmetic progression, is equal to $ \\text{addRothNumber}(\\text{range } n) $.",

    },

      "informal_description": "For any natural numbers $k$ and $n$, the sum of the $k$-th powers of the divisors of $n$ is zero if and only if $n$ is zero.",
      "path": "Mathlib.NumberTheory.ArithmeticFunction.Misc"
    },
    {

      "informal_name": "Equality of Roth Numbers for Initial Segment and Natural Number under Size Constraint",

      "informal_description": "For natural numbers $k$ and $n$ satisfying $2k \\leq n$, the Roth number of the initial segment $\\{0, 1, \\ldots, k-1\\}$ in the finite set $\\mathrm{Fin}(n+1)$ is equal to the Roth number of the natural number $k$.
